open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: A name is judged when the folder is observed.
open_points.question: At which exact event is the name fixed for this scan: directory listing, per-entry metadata read, file open, or another defined instant?
options: Fix the name and ignored status when the directory entry is listed.
Fix them when metadata for that entry is read.
Re-evaluate the current name when the file is opened.
open_points.default_guess: Fix the name and ignored status when the directory entry is listed.

witness.initial: An ordinary file is present in the photo folder while a scan is starting.
events: The scanner lists the folder and sees the ordinary name.
Syncthing renames the entry to a conflict-copy name before the scanner reads its metadata.
The scanner continues processing the entry.
outcomes: The listing was the observation, so the entry is treated as the observed ordinary name and later fails when that path cannot be read.
The metadata read was the observation, so the conflict-copy name is ignored and no observation is reported.
witness.observer: The calling flow reading the scan result

open_points.subject: A1
open_points.text: A file renamed after the observation is no longer at the observed path, so reading it for placing fails with `unreadable_file` (A3 rule 4).
open_points.question: What must happen if the observed path exists again at placement time—for example because the file was renamed away and back, or another file with the same content replaced it—and how is a past rename distinguished from an unchanged file?
options: Any detected change of directory-entry identity since observation causes `unreadable_file`.
Only the current path and content are checked; matching content may be placed.
A replacement is classified as `source_changed`, while an absent path is `unreadable_file`.
open_points.default_guess: Require the same observed file identity and content; return `unreadable_file` when the entry disappeared and `source_changed` when a different entry occupies the path.

witness.initial: A scan observes `a.jpg` with source hash H.
events: Syncthing renames `a.jpg` to a conflict-copy name.
Before placement, an entry named `a.jpg` containing the same bytes H appears again.
The calling flow requests placement of H.
outcomes: Placement is refused because the observed file was renamed after observation.
Placement succeeds because the observed path and source content currently match the scan.
witness.observer: The calling flow and the owner

open_points.subject: A1 INV-18
open_points.text: a conflict copy in the folder and in a subfolder, each with the mark in lower, upper and mixed case, is absent from the scan and placing it by its hash fails with `not_ready_or_absent` (`test_a_syncthing_conflict_copy_is_neither_offered_nor_placed`).
open_points.question: Must this test also assert that the failed placement creates no stored binary, placement record, or other write, as required to show that the conflict copy was not the source of a new placement?
options: Assert the refusal and that no binary, placement record, or other state was written.
open_points.default_guess: Assert the refusal and that all placement stores remain unchanged.

witness.initial: A project has no placement for hash H, and only a conflict-copy file contains H.
events: The calling flow requests placement of H.
The implementation writes a prepared binary and placement record but returns `not_ready_or_absent`.
outcomes: A test checking only the returned failure passes even though INV-18 is violated.
A test checking the stores fails because the conflict copy caused a new placement.
witness.observer: A later scan or repeated placement, and the storage administrator

open_points.subject: A1 INV-18
open_points.text: an ordinary file with the content of a conflict copy is placed (`test_an_ordinary_file_is_placed_when_a_conflict_copy_has_the_same_content`)
open_points.question: How must the test demonstrate that the ordinary file, rather than the ignored conflict copy with identical content, was the source read for the new placement?
options: Instrument file access or make the conflict-copy path unreadable and assert it is never opened.
Treat successful placement of the shared hash as sufficient regardless of which path was read.
open_points.default_guess: Make access to the conflict copy observable and assert that only the ordinary path is opened.

witness.initial: An ordinary file and a conflict-copy file contain identical bytes H, and H has no placement.
events: The scan reports only the ordinary file.
The calling flow requests placement of H.
The implementation searches current files by hash and opens the conflict copy first.
outcomes: Placement succeeds, so a result-only test passes although the conflict copy supplied the new placement.
A file-access-aware test fails because the ignored conflict copy was opened as the source.
witness.observer: The invariant test and, if the two files race or diverge during reading, the calling flow
